ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Gwen Ifill Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Three weeks of postmenopausal bleeding in a woman of 60: examination, office endometrial biopsy, transvaginal ultrasound, and gynecologic oncology review booked. Concerns: Spotting, then light bleeding on and off for about three weeks, eight years after her periods stopped; no pain; She does not want a wait-and-see answer: she knows that bleeding after menopause is sometimes put down to nothing, and she wants the cause found quickly and told plainly; She wants to keep working and to decide who is told. [S]

tr.td: Office endometrial biopsy with a suction catheter (Pipelle), with a chaperone, after verbal consent: adequate tissue obtained; tolerated with mild cramping

Transvaginal ultrasound of the pelvis: endometrium 16 mm, heterogeneous, with an irregular junction with the myometrium and internal blood flow; two small intramural fibroids (1.8 cm and 1.2 cm); ovaries normal for age; no free fluid

CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast: enlarged, heterogeneous uterine cavity; a 1.5 cm right external iliac lymph node and a 1.7 cm left para-aortic lymph node below the renal veins, both suspicious; no liver, lung, bone or peritoneal lesion; no ascites
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes

Robotic-assisted total laparoscopic hysterectomy with removal of both fallopian tubes and ovaries and pelvic washings. Pathology: endometrioid adenocarcinoma, FIGO grade 2 (low grade), 4.2 cm, invading 65% of the myometrial thickness; no cervical stromal invasion; focal (not substantial) lymphovascular space invasion; tubes, ovaries and serosa free; washings negative. Mismatch repair deficient (loss of MLH1 and PMS2), MLH1 promoter hypermethylated, POLE wild-type, p53 wild-type; estrogen receptor positive. FIGO 2013 stage IIIC2ii, molecular class MMRd
Sentinel lymph node mapping with indocyanine green, both sides of the pelvis: right external iliac sentinel node with a 9 mm metastasis; left obturator sentinel node negative on ultrastaging
Excision of the enlarged left para-aortic lymph node seen on CT, with adjacent para-aortic nodes below the renal veins: 1 of 4 nodes involved (14 mm deposit)

Genetic counseling: universal Lynch syndrome tumor screening explained; MLH1 and PMS2 loss explained by MLH1 promoter hypermethylation, which is acquired in the tumor and not inherited; germline testing not indicated; she was told what would change that advice

CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast at the end of combination treatment: no enlarged pelvic or para-aortic lymph node, no vaginal cuff mass, no liver, lung, bone or peritoneal lesion; expected postoperative changes (no evidence of disease)

tr.td: Three weeks of postmenopausal bleeding in a woman of 60: examination, office endometrial biopsy, transvaginal ultrasound, and gynecologic oncology review booked
Biopsy result: endometrial cancer; staging CT, gynecologic oncology consultation, Lynch syndrome tumor screening, and preparation for surgery
Review three weeks after surgical staging: final pathology and molecular class, genetic counseling, and the first cycle of dostarlimab with carboplatin and paclitaxel
Midpoint of combination treatment: blood counts, immune-related adverse event checks, neuropathy, and mood
End of combination treatment: response CT, immune-related hypothyroidism, the first maintenance dostarlimab dose, and the survivorship plan

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Gynecologic oncology consultation within two weeks to review the endometrial biopsy and ultrasound with her and plan treatment if cancer or atypical hyperplasia is found

Any bleeding after menopause is evaluated: speculum and bimanual examination, office endometrial biopsy at the first visit, and transvaginal ultrasound within the week, both done rather than relying on endometrial thickness alone; blood count and A1c; results by telephone within days, not at a routine visit

Staging and molecular classification: CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis; mismatch repair immunohistochemistry and p53 on the biopsy, with MLH1 promoter methylation testing for MLH1 loss and POLE sequencing on the surgical specimen; FIGO 2013 stage with the molecular class recorded

Robotic-assisted total laparoscopic hysterectomy with removal of both tubes and ovaries, pelvic washings, sentinel lymph node mapping with indocyanine green, and removal of the enlarged pelvic and para-aortic nodes

Lynch syndrome screening of the tumor for every endometrial cancer, with genetic counseling; germline testing if mismatch repair loss is not explained by MLH1 promoter methylation, and cascade testing offered to blood relatives only if a germline variant is found

Dostarlimab 500 mg with carboplatin (AUC 5) and paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 every three weeks for six cycles, then dostarlimab 1000 mg every six weeks for up to three years, for mismatch repair deficient stage IIIC2 disease; hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV screening first; three-drug antiemetic prevention; blood counts, kidney function and magnesium before each cycle; TSH, free T4, liver tests, glucose and morning cortisol at baseline and before each cycle; neuropathy checks at each visit
GL-NCCN-UTERINE-2026, GL-RUBY-2023, GL-JEMPERLI-LABEL, GL-ASCO-IRAE-2021, GL-ASCO-ANTIEMETIC-2020, GL-ASCO-CIPN-2020, GL-ASCO-HBV-2020, GL-CMID-2026
Immune-related hypothyroidism: levothyroxine with TSH and free T4 every six weeks, continuing dostarlimab

Survivorship: examination with a pelvic examination every three months for two years, CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis every six months for three years, no routine vaginal cytology and no CA-125 (normal at diagnosis), teaching on symptoms of recurrence, lymphedema checks, sexual health, weight, activity, blood pressure, lipid and glucose care, distress screening, and age-appropriate screening for other cancers
Distress and depression screening at each visit, plain explanations, written information, and support she chooses; she decides who receives each note
Endometrial tissue diagnosis and ultrasound within one week, and a gynecologic oncology plan within three weeks of presentation
Biopsy at the first visit, ultrasound in two days, result in four days, CT in eight, consultation at two weeks
Surgical staging within four weeks of diagnosis
Minimally invasive hysterectomy with sentinel node mapping and para-aortic node removal two weeks after the consultation
Six cycles of dostarlimab with carboplatin and paclitaxel every three weeks without a delay of more than one week
Six cycles on schedule; CT shows no evidence of disease
Lynch syndrome tumor screening completed and explained before treatment starts
MLH1 promoter hypermethylation found: acquired, not inherited; genetic counseling done
Immune-related adverse events found early: TSH, liver tests, glucose and cortisol checked on schedule
Hypothyroidism found on a scheduled TSH and treated without stopping dostarlimab; one missed baseline cortisol recorded and corrected
PHQ-9 below 10 throughout treatment, with support she chooses

Alert, direct and precise; asks pointed questions and wants the facts plainly; PHQ-2 negative; no thoughts of self-harm [S]
